chunks: And whatever in this book is narrated from Abu Hamzah Al-Thumali, I have transmitted it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr Al-Bazanti, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamzah Thabit ibn Dinar Al-Thumali.

Dinar is known by the kunya Abu Safiyyah. He was from a clan of Banu Tha'labah and was attributed to Thumalah because his residence was among them. He passed away in the year 150 AH. He was trustworthy and just (thiqa 'adl) and met four Imams: Ali ibn Al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them all). Although there are many transmission routes to him, I have sufficed with mentioning only one of them.

key_terms.أبو حمزة الثمالي: Abu Hamzah Al-Thumali, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: Who was Abu Hamzah Al-Thumali and what is his chain of narration in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a rigorous isnad verification for Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, highlighting his reliability (thiqah) and his unique distinction of having directly encountered four Imams, spanning from Ali ibn al-Husayn to Musa al-Kadhim. This biographical note underscores the continuity of the Shia scholarly chain (tawatur) and justifies the selection of this specific transmission path among many available, emphasizing the authenticity of the narrated traditions.
